config.title: Accordion

intro.title: Accordion
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive accordion component, a common UI element that allows users to expand and collapse sections of content. You will learn how to manage component state to track which accordion item is currently open. The main technologies and constructs involved include React's useState hook for state management and conditional rendering to show or hide content. By the end, you'll have a functional accordion that responds to user clicks, reinforcing fundamental React patterns in a practical project.
intro.usecase: Accordions are essential UI components for managing content density in modern web applications. You'll find them in FAQ sections where questions expand to reveal answers, in dashboard settings panels that organize configuration options into collapsible groups, and in mobile navigation menus that conserve screen space. As a React developer, implementing accordions helps you create intuitive interfaces that prevent information overload while maintaining accessibility and smooth user interactions across devices.

objectives: Initialize and manage the expanded state of an accordion item using React's useState hook.
Construct a reusable AccordionItem component that conditionally renders its content based on state.
Implement a click handler to toggle the visibility of the accordion content.
Apply conditional styling to dynamically update the accordion's visual indicators (like icons or borders) during state changes.
Render a complete accordion interface by composing multiple AccordionItem components with distinct data.
Control the accordion behavior to allow only one item to be open at a time (single-expand mode).
Integrate dynamic data (like an array of FAQs) to populate the accordion items programmatically.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React and useState are added to the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the Accordion component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Accordion that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name Accordion and have it return null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Accordion component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a component named Accordion that returns null.
successCriteria: A component named Accordion is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'Accordion' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'Accordion' and it returns null.

steps.title: Initialize accordion state
steps.instruction: Inside your Accordion component, declare a state variable called 'expandedIndex' using useState, initialized to null.
steps.hint: Call useState with null as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state variable for tracking selection
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'expandedIndex' that can track which accordion item is currently expanded.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call with null initial value, destructured into 'expandedIndex' and 'setExpandedIndex'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with null and destructuring the array into 'expandedIndex' and 'setExpandedIndex'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use useState(null) to create a state variable called 'expandedIndex'.

steps.title: Define accordion data
steps.instruction: Inside your Accordion component, create a constant array named 'items' containing objects with 'title' and 'content' properties. Add at least two items with sample accordion content.
steps.hint: Define the array before the return statement. Each object should have a title (string) and content (string).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a static data source for accordion items that will be used for rendering.
successCriteria: An array named 'items' is defined with at least two objects, each containing 'title' and 'content' string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your array is named 'items' and contains objects with both 'title' and 'content' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The items array isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a constant array with the correct structure.

steps.title: Add container structure
steps.instruction: Return a div container element from the Accordion component.
steps.hint: Replace the return null; statement with a div element that will wrap your accordion content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element instead of null, creating the basic structure for the accordion.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element as its root JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element from the component instead of null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element to create the accordion container structure.

steps.title: Map accordion items
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, map over the items array to create a list of accordion item divs.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the items array to generate JSX elements for each item.
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion container now contains a mapped list of item divs, each with a unique key.
successCriteria: The items array is mapped inside the container div
Each mapped element has a key prop
The mapping returns JSX elements for each item
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started mapping, but check that you're returning JSX elements with proper keys for each item.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mapping isn't implemented correctly. Make sure to use the map method on the items array inside the container div.

steps.title: Add item title and click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the map callback, add a div element for each item's title. Set its onClick handler to call the toggle function with the current index.
steps.hint: The div should display the item's title and call the toggle handler when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each accordion item will have a clickable title that triggers the toggle handler.
successCriteria: A div element is added inside the map callback, displaying the item's title and wired to handleToggle with the current index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the onClick handler calls handleToggle with the index parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The title element or click handler is missing. Add a div with onClick that calls handleToggle(index).

steps.title: Add basic styling classes
steps.instruction: Add className attributes to the accordion container, each item, the title div, and the content div for basic visual styling.
steps.hint: Assign appropriate class names like 'accordion', 'accordion-item', 'accordion-title', and 'accordion-content' to the JSX elements.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding CSS classes to elements

Title

Content
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion structure now has CSS class names on all major elements, ready for styling.
successCriteria: The container div has className='accordion', each item div has className='accordion-item', the title div has className='accordion-title', and the conditional content div has className='accordion-content'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some class names, but check that all four elements (container, item, title, content) have their respective className attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS classes are missing or incorrect. Make sure to add className attributes to the container, each item, the title div, and the content div with appropriate values.
